frontier.hypothesis: The counter allocno can reach n_refs >= 6 at the pre-call live_length of 13 (pri 2*6/13 = 9230 > h's 8750) if the loop carries front-end loop NOTES, because flow.c weights each ref by loop_depth - but only if a shape exists that re-weights the COUNTER's in-loop refs without equally re-weighting h's in-loop `slt` use.
frontier.mechanism: tools/gcc-2.7.2/flow.c:2081/2329/2515/2725 `reg_n_refs[regno] += loop_depth`, with loop_depth from basic_block_loop_depth set at :1385/:1401/:1447 off NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG, which the C front end emits only for real for/while/do statements - never for goto-formed loops. Naive re-weighting takes the counter to ~7 refs (pri 10769) but h to ~8-9 refs (pri 15000+), i.e. it loses; the question is whether the exit test can be arranged so h is not read at the deeper depth.

frontier.hypothesis: Target's `move s0,zero` in the `jal rand` delay slot may not have come from a literal pre-call `i = 0;` statement at all - reorg.c's backward search could have pulled a DIFFERENT insn, or the counter's zero could originate from a different C construct whose allocno is short-lived.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c:fill_simple_delay_slots fills a CALL_INSN's slot by a backward search over the preceding insns in the same block; any insn that does not set a register the call needs is eligible. Every session so far has assumed the eligible insn must be the counter's initialisation, which is what forces the counter's live range across the call and loses the 8888-vs-8750 tie.
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS modality: `cc1 <flags> -dd` on the floor-2 form and on the pre-call form; read the .dbr dump around the `jal rand` and enumerate what the backward search actually considered and rejected.
